description: Table 3 is a single rendered table image (no micrographs or plots) listing tensile mechanical properties of Nb-containing medium-Mn low-density steels aged at 723 K for different periods. It has five columns: "Samples", "Aging states", "Yield strength [MPa]", "Tensile strength [MPa]" and "Total elongation [%]", and four data rows grouped by two sample rows. The "Samples" column is row-merged: "0.02Nb steels" spans the first two data rows and "0.04Nb steels" the last two. For 0.02Nb steels: 723 K/6 h gives yield strength 950 ± 14 MPa, tensile strength 1081 ± 18 MPa and total elongation 28 ± 1 %; 723 K/9 h gives 975 ± 5 MPa, 1029 ± 4 MPa and 8 ± 2 %. For 0.04Nb steels: 723 K/6 h gives 1010 ± 4 MPa, 1104 ± 5 MPa and 17 ± 1 %; 723 K/9 h gives 1019 ± 3 MPa, 1072 ± 3 MPa and 5 ± 1 %. Every value carries a ± standard deviation. The table shows that raising Nb from 0.02 to 0.04 wt.% increases both yield and tensile strength at each aging time, while extending aging from 6 h to 9 h raises yield strength slightly but lowers tensile strength and causes a sharp drop in total elongation (28→8 % for 0.02Nb; 17→5 % for 0.04Nb). All numbers are printed in the table cells; the image adds no graphical content.

observations.observation: The table has five columns: Samples, Aging states, Yield strength [MPa], Tensile strength [MPa] and Total elongation [%].
0.02Nb steels aged at 723 K/6 h show yield strength 950 ± 14 MPa, tensile strength 1081 ± 18 MPa and total elongation 28 ± 1 %.
0.02Nb steels aged at 723 K/9 h show yield strength 975 ± 5 MPa, tensile strength 1029 ± 4 MPa and total elongation 8 ± 2 %.
0.04Nb steels aged at 723 K/6 h show yield strength 1010 ± 4 MPa, tensile strength 1104 ± 5 MPa and total elongation 17 ± 1 %.
0.04Nb steels aged at 723 K/9 h show yield strength 1019 ± 3 MPa, tensile strength 1072 ± 3 MPa and total elongation 5 ± 1 %.
Every entry in the table is reported with a ± uncertainty (standard deviation).
At both aging times the 0.04Nb steels have higher yield strength and higher tensile strength than the 0.02Nb steels.
For both Nb contents, increasing aging time from 6 h to 9 h raises yield strength slightly (950→975 MPa for 0.02Nb; 1010→1019 MPa for 0.04Nb) but lowers tensile strength.
Total elongation collapses on going from 723 K/6 h to 723 K/9 h in both steels, from 28 ± 1 % to 8 ± 2 % (0.02Nb) and from 17 ± 1 % to 5 ± 1 % (0.04Nb).
The table presents tensile mechanical properties of Nb-containing steels aged at 723 K for different periods.
The caption identifies the alloy systems as 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels; the paper abstract describes them as Fe-12Mn-9Al-3Cr-1.4C-0.02/0.04Nb low-density steels.
